native_findings.observed: Business directory must contain product name. If requested Hermes bytecode/config is absent, an existing rn_business.jsbundle selects V5. Business dependencies resolve as siblings of the business directory. Native V5 success returns1 when original Hermes flag was true, otherwise0.
Parses rn_business.jsbundle directly with a product_packageID_jsc key; no generated _crn_config is required.
__open_2 flags0 and fopen mode r with fread; bundle and resource indexes are allocated in memory. No filesystem writes in reviewed V5 parse and resource-access path.
Resource/module slices are read from in-memory BundleUnit data; no generated files.

implementation_decisions: Use revision directory as sibling of the normal schedule directory to preserve existing common-dependency lookup.
Leave original CRNURL strings, query maps, product names, package IDs and Hermes flag unchanged.
Redirect final Java/native business load after cache/server package selection, including preloadV1 and V2.
Redirect module path to exact isolated indexed JS so combined-bundle resources use the same source.
Initialize Java resource bundle key for successful raw fallback result1 only when the path is the confirmed revision; preserve result1 return for the existing caller MIXED transition.
Extract original-named patched APK7z through existing verified Un7zUtil ABI, validate SHA-256 every load, stage privately and rename atomically.
Reject duplicate hooks, mismatched ABIs/register layouts, symlinked destination/lock, unknown archive members, and invalid bytes before redirecting.
limitations: No Android device executed and no user on-device cache was read.

Fail-open behavior applies to context, path setup, extraction, reflection, or integrity failure before redirection. Native parse failures after successful redirection still follow the original app retry/error handling.
Existing common dependencies and server-selected package IDs are retained. Their actual in-device compatibility is not runtime-tested.
